title: Each screen has one obvious primary action
note: One control per screen is visibly the main thing to do; secondary actions are quieter.
intent: When three buttons look equally important, a person has to read all of them. Pick the single action the screen exists for and give it the accent colour and the most visual weight; secondary actions use an outline or a text style, destructive ones are quiet until confirmed. Put the primary action where the eye finishes reading (end of the form, top right of the toolbar) and give it a verb that says what happens ("Save changes", not "OK"). Keep one filled button per view.

check.ask: Is it obvious which single control is the main thing to do on this screen, with the other actions visibly quieter?
check.note: One control is visibly the primary action of the screen.

port: styles.css defines .button (quiet) and .button.primary (accent) once; components choose one, and a view never contains two primaries.
